data.question: Does the PreToolUse guard refuse the read-only 'git stash list'/'git stash show'?

evidence.note: CONFIRMED: before the fix, `git stash list`/`git stash show`/`git stash show stash@{0}` each return a Refusal (entry `git stash`); exempting the read-only list/show subcommands in _matches_head makes all 49 test_forbidden_commands.py tests pass (3 were refused before). Research R21ce48633b.

Loaded project rules via `ddflow brief --item». r-gemini-key-load governs the review gate (GEMINI_API_KEY already exported into this shell before review). r-task-phase-needs-wave: the item carries a wave tag. No rule forbids allowing a read-only read of the shared stash; the entry stays, only its prefix match is narrowed to writing verbs.

Implemented in the worktree: ddflow/services/forbidden.py now treats git stash` list/show as read-only (no Refusal) via _git_subcommand_matches + _STASH_READONLY; writing verbs (push/pop/branch, bare stash) still refuse. Regression: tests/test_forbidden_commands.py (git stash list/show added to test_allowed) 49 passed.

chunk_findings.detail: The read-only stash exemption is applied whenever the forbidden entry's first word after `git` is `stash`, even when the entry explicitly forbids the read-only subcommand itself. For example, with `[hooks].forbidden_commands = ["git stash list"]`, the command `git stash list` reaches `_git_subcommand_matches(["stash","list"], ["stash","list"])`, which returns `False` because `args[1] == "list"` is in `_STASH_READONLY`; the command is therefore allowed even though it is explicitly forbidden. Before this change it was blocked. The exemption should only apply when the configured entry is exactly the generic `git stash` (e.g. `want == ["stash"]`), not when `want` itself names `list`/`show`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_git_subcommand_matches

chunk_findings.detail: The read-only exemption is incomplete for non-writing read-only invocations. With `[hooks].forbidden_commands = ["git stash"]`, the command `git stash --help` (and `git stash -h`) still returns a forbidden-command refusal: `_git_subcommand_matches(["stash"], ["stash", "--help"])` returns `True` because `"--help"` is not in `_STASH_READONLY`. This contradicts the stated expected behavior to “refuse the writing verbs only.”

The added tests only cover top-level `git stash -h`/`--help`, so the stated “refuse the writing verbs only” behavior is still incomplete.

chunk_findings.detail: The new read-only exemption treats any token `-h` or `--help` after `stash` as a help flag: `if rest and (rest[0] in _STASH_READONLY or "-h" in rest or "--help" in rest): return False`. That lets a WRITING stash verb through when the token is not a help flag. For example, `git stash push -- --help` yields `rest = ["push", "--", "--help"]`, so `"--help" in rest` is true and `_git_subcommand_matches` returns False, meaning `[hooks].forbidden_commands 'git stash'` does not refuse it; Git then actually executes `stash push` with `--help` as a pathspec after `--`, writing to the shared stash stack. The same bypass exists for `git stash push -m -h` / `--message --help`, where `-m` consumes the next token as the message value. The condition must only recognize `-h`/`--help` as help when they are actual options, not after `--` or after an option that consumes an argument.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:252

chunk_findings.detail: Treating any `-h`/`--help` token after `stash` as read-only lets writing verbs through. `_git_subcommand_matches(["stash"], ["stash", "push", "-m", "--help"])` and `["stash", "push", "--", "--help"]` both hit `"-h" in rest or "--help" in rest` and return False, so the hook allows them. Git does not: `-m`/`--message` consume the next argv element as the message (even if it looks like a flag), and `--` ends option parsing so the following `--help` is a pathspec. Either command updates the shared stash (`git stash push -m --help`, or `git stash push -- --help` when that path has changes) instead of printing help and exiting. The new `git stash pop --help` case is fine only when the token is actually a help flag, not an option value or a post-`--` pathspec.
